quote: Yeah. No. What I do is I just confirm the information that I do have, and then, yeah, I can get started on the design.
stewart_read: Rep handled the repeat-contact complaint with specificity and action rather than defending the call, which is the correct protocol move per the schema's honest_specificity pattern.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example worth reinforcing — the rep resolved friction via action, not argument, and should be told explicitly that this was the right move.

quote: Do you know how much you're paying on average a month on that eleven month?
stewart_read: Rep captured the bill figure but the flip into emotional alignment-against-the-utility never happens; the customer's own comment 'Oh, wow. Okay' at 01:52 (attributed to the rep in the transcript, likely a diarization artifact) suggests some reaction to the $300 figure but no anchoring line follows from the rep.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intended the pause after quoting the range back ('80 to $2.60. Okay. Yeah. Alrighty.') as an implicit acknowledgment, but this is passive restatement, not a flip.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to turn the $300 spike or the $80-260 range into a direct statement of cost pain ('that's money going to the utility with nothing to show for it') before moving to the credit qualifier.

quote: I think so. You can check if you want.
stewart_read: Customer offers to let the rep verify his credit rather than self-report, and the rep declines the offer ('No. That's okay. I believe you.'). Per Spencer's operator note, self-reported credit is unreliable and this is a case where the rep could have taken the more reliable path but didn't need to since he wasn't DQing anyway.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep missed a chance to increase confidence in the qualifier. Strategic read: since the answer wasn't a DQ either way (rep proceeded), this had no material impact on the call outcome.
coaching_implication: Low priority — worth noting only because it illustrates the rep taking self-report at face value, consistent with the schema's stated_vs_pulled credit tension for Kenny to resolve.

quote: If you just had warned me that you need the thing, I would have brought it in the office or one second.
stewart_read: Customer voices a specific, reasonable complaint that he wasn't told in advance to have his bill ready, and there is no rep acknowledgment captured before the multi-minute gap. This is a general process-friction/acknowledgment gap, not a vulnerability disclosure (health/financial/family loss) — it does not map to coaching_philosophy.empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep didn't respond because the transcript may have truncated a real acknowledgment during the gap. Strategic read: none apparent — this looks like a missed real-time acknowledgment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally acknowledge process complaints in the moment ('you're right, I should have flagged that before we started') rather than silently continuing, especially when the customer is audibly working through friction live on the call.

quote: I I don't want to be doing this while somebody's looking over my shoulder. Can can we be more organized a little bit?
stewart_read: The customer proposes ending the live struggle and doing this later; the rep agrees but locks nothing beyond a text message and 'whenever you get home today.' No specific callback time, no confirmed appointment slot, no 'is that fair?' handshake.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be reading the customer's visible frustration and choosing not to push for a hard time to avoid further irritation. But the schema's button_up discipline requires a locked next step even under friction — a specific time window could still have been offered gently.
coaching_implication: This is the priority coaching moment: rep should have proposed a concrete follow-up time ('I'll call you back at 6 tonight once you're home — does that work?') instead of leaving it as 'whenever you get home today.'

quote: Yes. No problem. So what I can do is I can just send you a text message. And then whenever you get home today, if you could just send over that photo, then, yeah, we can finish up the estimate for you.
stewart_read: This is the correct alternative-path pivot in method (text follow-up for the bill), but it closes the call without a locked appointment or callback time — no day/time was ever set for a closer appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may be treating this as a natural extension of the existing paid/organic-lead bill-collection allowance, planning to follow up once the bill arrives. Reactive read: the rep let the call end without owning any concrete next step, which is a fragile non-booking.
coaching_implication: Manager should flag this as a call that ended without a booked appointment — the rep needs a habit of proposing an appointment time even when the bill isn't in hand yet, since Ion's bill_collection rules allow booking pending the bill.

quote: We we just got the bill, today, and, I think we we had, 300 today, I think, I believe.
stewart_read: The customer volunteers that his bill just came in unusually high ($300 vs. a stated average of $80-260), an immediate bill-pain data point delivered fresh on the call — a strong anchor opportunity.
coaching_implication: Rep should have anchored directly on this fresh spike ('so today's bill alone was already above your normal high end — that's exactly the kind of increase our program targets') rather than moving straight to the credit qualifier.

quote: I'm just creating my account in, Dominion right now. So I I think we can we can do it. We can do this thing tomorrow.
stewart_read: After a long unexplained gap, the customer offers to continue tomorrow rather than push through — an opening for the rep to build urgency or curiosity about the design (e.g., referencing the $300 spike) to keep momentum, which the rep does not attempt.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep missed a chance to re-anchor urgency. Strategic read: given the customer's visible frustration ('looking over my shoulder'), pushing further in the moment might have backfired — deferring may have been the lower-risk move.
coaching_implication: When a customer proposes deferring, coach the rep to at least re-state the bill pain briefly before agreeing, to keep the reason for urgency alive into the callback.
